teaser: My 2018 book for young developers, 60% done, its outlines since written here as articles, and an AI edition, dated October 2026, made first.
core_idea: Generation Z Developers (2018) holds much of what the newsroom now argues, mostly as outlines since written as articles, so an AI edition dated October 2026 keeps the name because everyone now has to be a developer, frames the reader with explorers, villagers and town planners, and is made first, by review, an editor agent interviewing Dinis, quick public iterations and KDP.

figures.caption: From the 2018 book to the 2026 articles. On the left, chapters of Generation Z Developers: five left as outlines in 2018 (pioneers, settlers and town planners; graphs; your future self; publish, publish, publish; GitHub as your CV) and two that were written (machine learning and AI; open source). On the right, the newsroom articles that have since written each one: software vendors as villagers and explorer coding; the graphs books and search as navigation; bringing my past work back; your own newsroom; act as the job you want; hired for the workflow; the fork next door. Of the book's 138 files, 90 are still outlines.

The printed early release of Generation Z Developers, September 2018: "Key concepts and ideas for the next generation of developers", and seven lines on the cover: question everything; make fact based decisions; understand the history of tech; learn how to learn; understand what game is being played; develop intellectual curiosity; shake things up.
